dn15:24.5: They describe the self in the present as formed and infinite; or they describe it as sure to be in some other place formed and infinite; or else they think: ‘Though it is not like that, I will ensure it is provided with what it needs to become like that.’
dn15:24.6: This being so, it’s appropriate to say that a theory of self as formed and infinite underlies them.
dn15:24.8: They describe the self in the present as formless and limited; or they describe it as sure to be in some other place formless and limited; or else they think: ‘Though it is not like that, I will ensure it is provided with what it needs to become like that.’
dn15:24.9: This being so, it’s appropriate to say that a theory of self as formless and limited underlies them.
dn15:26.2: They don’t describe the self in the present as formed and limited; or as sure to become in some other place formed and limited; and they don’t think: ‘Though it is not like that, I will ensure it is provided with what it needs to become like that.’
dn15:26.3: This being so, it’s appropriate to say that a theory of self as formed and limited doesn’t underlie them.
dn15:26.5: They don’t describe the self in the present as formed and infinite; or as sure to become in some other place formed and infinite; and they don’t think: ‘Though it is not like that, I will ensure it is provided with what it needs to become like that.’
dn15:26.6: This being so, it’s appropriate to say that a theory of self as formed and infinite doesn’t underlie them.
dn15:26.8: They don’t describe the self in the present as formless and limited; or as sure to become in some other place formless and limited; and they don’t think: ‘Though it is not like that, I will ensure it is provided with what it needs to become like that.’
dn15:26.9: This being so, it’s appropriate to say that a theory of self as formless and limited doesn’t underlie them.
dn15:29.2: Painful feelings are impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
dn15:29.3: Neutral feelings are impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
dn15:34.4: “Now, Ānanda, as for the dimension of non-percipient beings:
dn15:34.5: Is it appropriate for someone who understands it—and its origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape—to take pleasure in it?”
dn15:34.7: “Now, Ānanda, as for the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception:
dn15:34.8: Is it appropriate for someone who understands it—and its origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape—to take pleasure in it?”
dn15:36.6: The Great Discourse on Causation is finished—the second.
